title: batchDiafilter operation
description: A stirred RETENTATE vessel behind a membrane (choupoBatch): the batch half of the pressure-driven separation the steady spiralWoundModule solves. It adds no architecture — the same TransportModel::localFluxes (solutionDiffusion or DSPM-DE), the same membrane asset record and osmotic block, asked once per instant instead of once per channel node. Well mixed, so one bulk composition; the permeate's solvent is closed on the declared solution density the concentrations were built from, so the vessel conserves mass to machine precision. Two modes: `concentration` (no make-up, the vessel shrinks) and `constantVolume` (diafiltrate added at the permeate rate, solutes wash out; the make-up is ledgered under its own kind word externalIntake). The unit publishes the OBSERVED rejection R_obs_<solute> at every instant and, in constantVolume mode, washoutActual_<solute> beside washoutIdeal_<solute> — the ideal evaluated from this run's own initial R, computed and never declared, so the gap between the hand derivation c/c0 = exp(-(1-R)N) and the run cannot have been arranged. Initial holdup comes from 0/internalStates/<unit>, a `holdup {}` block (an inline initial{} is refused). The pump work is NOT ledgered: energyLedgerGap names it and the campaign energy balance stays UNAVAILABLE.

membrane.title: Membrane asset record
membrane.description: Name of the curated membrane record (data/standards/assets/, kind membrane) whose permeabilities the transport law reads.

transport.title: Local transport law
transport.description: The same local flux law the steady module uses; DSPM-DE needs the record's pore data and a charged feed.

transportParameters.title: Transport-law parameters
transportParameters.description: Optional block handed verbatim to the chosen transport law's readParameters. `DSPM-DE` reads `poreSolver { method finiteDifference | closedForm; nodes <n>; wallClosure porePermeate | solutionDiffusion; }`, `hindrance DechadilokDeen2006;`, `activity wallDavies | ideal | bulkOverPoreDavies;` and `bulkDielectric <eps>;` -- and nothing else (an unknown key or word refuses).

poreSolver.title: DSPM-DE pore solver
poreSolver.description: How DSPM-DE crosses the pore.  Absent = the pore SOLVED (the default since 2026-10-24): `finiteDifference` on 101 nodes with `wallClosure porePermeate`, each default announced.  `finiteDifference` SOLVES the extended Nernst-Planck equations on `nodes` grid points across the pore (faces included), electroneutrality at every node and zero current, every node at once by Newton on the declared block-tridiagonal structure -- NanoFiltran's method (Geraldes & Alves 2008).  `nodes` defaults to 101, announced; it refuses with `closedForm`, and an unknown method word refuses.  `wallClosure` (finiteDifference only): `porePermeate` (default) closes the multi-ionic wall with the solved pore's own permeate, the wall and the pore converged together by Newton (NanoFiltran solves them in one matrix); `solutionDiffusion` closes it with the salts' solution-diffusion B_s.  `closedForm` (the default until 2026-10-24, now only DECLARED): the pore is NOT solved -- feed-face Donnan, an electroneutral permeate, each ion carried across alone by a closed-form transmission that is not the solution of the Nernst-Planck equations (it tends to K_c > 1 at low Peclet number), its wall closed with B_s.

hindrance.title: DSPM-DE hindrance factors
hindrance.description: Absent = `DechadilokDeen2006`, the one pair (announced as the default): K_d = H/Phi (lambda <= 0.95; 0.984((1-lambda)/lambda)^2.5 above) and K_c their rational fit -- the cross-section-averaged pair (Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 45 (2006) 6953).  H, the Dechadilok-Deen polynomial, is Phi K_d.  `legacy` (H itself taken as K_d, so the steric partition counted twice in diffusion; the default until 2026-10-24) REFUSES by name, saying why.

activity.title: DSPM-DE activity treatment
activity.description: Absent = `wallDavies`: Davies at the bulk ionic strength on the feed face, the permeate ideal.  `ideal`: every activity coefficient 1.  `bulkOverPoreDavies`: gamma_bulk/gamma_pore at BOTH faces, Davies (log10) with A(eps, T) = 1.82483e6 (eps T)^-1.5 -- eps_b on the solution side, eps_p on the pore side, the pore gammas at the pore's end nodes; requires the solved pore (the default; refused with `method closedForm;`).

bulkDielectric.title: Bulk dielectric constant
bulkDielectric.description: The solution's relative dielectric constant in the Born term and in A(eps_b).  Absent = SolventProperties::epsWater(T) (78.45 at 25 C).

mode.title: Operating mode
mode.description: `concentration`: Q_d = 0, the vessel shrinks and solutes concentrate. `constantVolume`: Q_d = Q_p, solvent made up as fast as it permeates and solutes wash out.

P_feed.title: Feed-side pressure
P_feed.description: Retentate-side pressure; the transmembrane pressure is P_feed - P_permeate.

rho.title: Solution density
rho.description: Declared, never defaulted: the density the concentrations and the permeate mass closure are both built on (BulkConversion.H).

rho_diafiltrate.title: Diafiltrate density
rho_diafiltrate.description: Density of the make-up solvent in constantVolume mode; defaults to rho when omitted.

k_film.title: Film mass-transfer coefficient
k_film.description: Concentration-polarisation coefficient, DECLARED by the case: the unit refuses without it rather than inventing a correlation for a stirred geometry it was not told.

osmotic.title: Osmotic pressure model
osmotic.description: The same block the steady module reads: `model vanHoff;` or `model pitzer;`.

fouling.title: Fouling (Hermia blocking law)
fouling.description: OPTIONAL. Resistance in series on the permeance handed to the transport law, 1/A_eff = 1/A_w + r_f(v), v = V_permeated/A, applied where the transport context is assembled so both laws see it. Absent the block there is no fouling and the run is byte-identical. A blocking law is a claim about a MECHANISM, so `reason` is required; `standard` and `complete` refuse by name (pore-internal geometry a lumped permeance cannot represent).

law.title: Blocking law
law.description: `cake`: r_f = k v (a deposited layer). `intermediate`: 1/A_eff = exp(k v)/A_w (progressive pore covering).

k.title: Fouling constant
k.description: EQUIPMENT-AND-FEED data (a rig and a material): declared in the case, never on a catalogue record; nothing here predicts it.

reason.title: Why this law fits this feed
reason.description: Required: the author states in writing why a deposited layer (cake) or covered pores (intermediate) describes this material.
